**The meaning of the verses**
﴿إِذْ أَوَى الْفِتْيَةُ إِلَى الْكَهْفِ فَقَالُوا رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا﴾
Remember, O Messenger, when the believing young men took refuge in the cave, fearing that their people would turn them from their faith and force them to worship idols. They said: "Our Lord, give us mercy from Yourself, by which You keep us firm and protect us from evil, and make easy for us the right path that leads us to the deeds You love, so that we are rightly guided and not astray."

﴿نَّحْنُ نَقُصُّ عَلَيْكَ نَبَأَهُم بِالْحَقِّ ۚ إِنَّهُمْ فِتْيَةٌ آمَنُوا بِرَبِّهِمْ وَزِدْنَاهُمْ هُدًى﴾
We relate to you, O Messenger, their story in truth. The People of the Cave were young men who believed in their Lord and obeyed His command, and We increased them in guidance and steadfastness on the truth. We strengthened their hearts with faith and made their resolve firm by it, when they stood before the disbelieving king as he blamed them for abandoning the worship of idols, and they said to him: "Our Lord, whom we worship, is the Lord of the heavens and the earth. We will never worship any other god besides Him. If we said anything else, we would have said something outrageous and far from the truth."

📖 At-Tafsir Al-Muyassar — King Fahd Complex.

**Talk with your child**
1. Why did the young men leave their city, carrying no food and no money? And what did they have with them?
2. What du'a did they make at the entrance of the cave? And how did Allah protect them while they slept? (The sun turned away from them, the dog was at the entrance, and they slept three hundred and nine years as if it were one day.)
3. Does "Whoever is mindful of Allah, Allah protects him" mean that a believer is never harmed? (No; a believer may be tested, but Allah protects his religion for him, helps him, and guides him rightly in his affair.)

**This week's exercise**
Your child memorises the young men's du'a: ﴿رَبَّنَا آتِنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحْمَةً وَهَيِّئْ لَنَا مِنْ أَمْرِنَا رَشَدًا﴾ (Our Lord, grant us mercy from Yourself, and guide us rightly in our affair), and says it this week before anything that worries them: a test, an appointment or a new place. At the end of the week, they tell you when they said it.
